digest.component_or_area: rebar doctor command (link audit / graph repair)
propositions: LINK events written before comparability became structural remain wrong on disk and distort ready/next-batch scheduling; an epic blocked by its own child or a cousin edge keeps propagating incorrectly through the dependency cascade.

The doctor command scans all net-active blocking edges against the current resolver rule, classifying findings as ancestor-blocking, mis-escalated, or unreadable, and can repair superset-safe replacements by writing new links before removing stale ones.

The repair path refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight, takes no outer store lock (each event write acquires its own), writes a pre-doctor-repair tag at pre-run OID as a rollback anchor, and declines ambiguous pairs whose unlink would cancel a different relation.

Repair status unrepairable edges (cyclic replacements, closed-source mis-escalations) remain on disk with both original links intact, do not stop the run, and exit code 1; edges with all closed endpoints do not affect scheduling.
A read-only scan (init_only=True) does not trigger store reconvergence; --repair --dry-run reports findings without writing events.

Live-run attestation: 18 edges found on this repository tracker (9 ancestor-blocking, 9 mis-escalated); 12 repaired (all 9 ancestor-blocking + 3 mis-escalated); 8 residuals all have closed blocked-sides and are provably inert to scheduling.
